stories.title: Cancer cells disrupt immune system coordination
stories.summary: The immune system relies on a network of cells that recognize danger and rally reinforcements to fight disease. New research indicates that cancer can evade this attack by specifically disrupting the teamwork required between these immune components. The body is essentially being told to stop talking to itself.

stories.title: Artificial protein activates faulty insulin receptors
stories.summary: Genetic mutations can leave insulin receptors unable to respond to chemical signals, preventing them from performing their function. A study in Science Translational Medicine reports that an artificial protein can now activate these mutated receptors to lower blood sugar in mice. The protein acts as a bypass.

stories.title: Ultrasound maps 3D blood flow in human kidney
stories.summary: Researchers at the Inserm Institute of Physics for Medicine have visualized the entire vascular network and blood flow of a human kidney in 3D. The team used a new ultrasound technique to map the organ. The method aims to improve the diagnosis of kidney diseases linked to vascular defects.

stories.title: Evolut PRO heart valve shows low reintervention rates
stories.summary: Five-year outcomes from the FORWARD PRO study show that patients treated with the Evolut PRO transcatheter aortic valve replacement system experienced low rates of reintervention. The trial tracked clinical endpoints across 39 centers in 14 European countries to evaluate the long-term durability and safety of the device.

stories.title: New map tracks gene splicing in brain cells
stories.summary: Alternative splicing allows the same gene to produce different RNA molecules, known as isoforms, which can then result in different proteins. A new map reveals how individual brain cells utilize these different RNA versions. The complexity of the process is now being charted at the cellular level.

stories.title: Four factors precede 99% of cardiovascular events
stories.summary: A study of 9 million people found that 99% of cardiovascular events were preceded by at least one of four factors: high blood pressure, cholesterol, blood glucose, or smoking. High blood pressure was the most frequent precursor, appearing in 93% of cases. The heart is rarely surprised.

stories.title: Brain circuit identified for sensory hypersensitivity
stories.summary: For many people with autism spectrum disorder, ordinary sensory experiences can feel overwhelming or intense. Researchers have identified a specific brain circuit that may be responsible for this sensory hypersensitivity. A light touch can now be traced to a specific neural pathway.

stories.title: Heart regeneration limited by beating trade-off
stories.summary: The human heart pumps blood over 100,000 times a day but struggles to repair itself after injury. Researchers at the Centro Nacional de Investigaciones Cardiovasculares Carlos III suggest this is due to a fundamental trade-off between the organ's constant beating and its capacity for cellular regeneration.

stories.title: Engineered antibiotics may expand drug options
stories.summary: MIT researchers have developed a method to improve the safety profiles of antimicrobial drugs that were previously discarded. The team hopes this engineering approach will expand the pool of available antibiotic candidates as more bacterial strains develop resistance to existing treatments. Old medicine is getting a second look.

stories.title: Nearly Two-Thirds of Indian Teenagers Lack Vitamin B12, Finds ICMR Survey - NDTV
ICMR survey finds high B12 deficiency in teens
stories.summary: The ICMR-NIN SAMPADA survey reports that nearly two-thirds of Indian teenagers are deficient in vitamin B12. Data shows a 66.1 percent prevalence rate among boys and 65.4 percent among girls. The findings suggest that nutritional challenges in the region extend well beyond simple caloric intake.

stories.title: ICMR survey reports widespread B12 deficiency
stories.summary: A national survey by the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition found vitamin B12 deficiency in 66.1 percent of Indian boys and 65.4 percent of girls aged 10 to 19. Deficiency was defined as serum levels below 203 pg/mL. The results highlight a significant nutritional gap in the adolescent population.

stories.title: ICMR survey reports anaemia rates in women
stories.summary: The ICMR SAMPADA survey found that 56% of Indian women of reproductive age are anaemic. The study, which covered over 2 lakh people, also noted that 46% of adolescent girls and 22 to 23% of adolescent boys are anaemic. The data reflects health markers across 183 districts.

stories.title: Assam records high anaemia prevalence
stories.summary: Assam has recorded some of the highest anaemia prevalence rates in India, according to an ICMR survey. The state reported 72.8 percent prevalence in adult women and 74 percent in men aged 60 and above. These figures significantly exceed the national averages for those respective age groups.

stories.title: ICMR survey shows lower anaemia prevalence
stories.summary: The ICMR SAMPADA 2023-2025 survey reports an overall lower prevalence of anaemia compared to previous national estimates. The study found 42 percent prevalence in children aged 12 to 59 months and 46 percent in adolescent girls. The data provides a new baseline for national health markers.

stories.title: Andhra Pradesh reports high anaemia in elderly women
stories.summary: An ICMR-NIN survey found that 81.7% of women aged 60 and above in Andhra Pradesh are anaemic, the highest rate among states surveyed. This figure is significantly higher than the national average of 55.7%. The state also recorded the highest anaemia rates for children below five.

stories.title: Anaemia remains high in Andhra Pradesh
stories.summary: The ICMR-NIN SAMPADA survey found that 81.7% of women aged 60 and above in Andhra Pradesh are anaemic, compared to a national average of 55.7%. The study highlights that anaemia remains a major public health concern in the state, with prevalence rates exceeding national figures across most groups.

stories.title: ICMR survey finds lower anaemia levels
stories.summary: The ICMR SAMPADA survey reports lower anaemia prevalence across India than earlier national estimates. The study, which analyzed over 170,000 blood samples, found that severe cases account for less than 2% of the population across most age groups. Targeted screening is now being recommended for specific groups.

stories.title: mRNA Ebola vaccine trial starts in Uganda
stories.summary: Trials of an experimental Ebola vaccine targeting the strain behind the current Democratic Republic of Congo outbreak have begun in Uganda. The country's virus research institute confirmed the start of the study on Friday. The vaccine aims to address the strain currently circulating in the region.

stories.title: Ugandan study outlines stepped care mental health framework after Ebola
stories.summary: Researchers in Uganda have developed a collaborative stepped-care mental health model to address the psychological consequences of Ebola outbreaks in low-resource settings. The project used a participatory methodology to build an intervention pathway following the 2022 epidemic. The initiative seeks to counter the long-term community burden of the disease.

stories.title: Egypt identified 27 victims of deadly Warraq Ring Road fire: Health Ministry - Health - Egypt - Ahram Online
Warraq fire kills 31 in Egypt
stories.summary: A fuel truck crash on the Ring Road in Giza killed 31 people and injured 21 on Wednesday. The Public Prosecution has opened an investigation into the incident, which also destroyed 27 vehicles. The cabinet plans to review fuel transport regulations once the cause is established.

stories.title: Atleast 30 killed, 15 injured in Giza Tunnel fire: Egypt Health Ministry
stories.summary: EGYPT: At least 30 people were killed and 15 others injured in a fire that broke out above the Ashara Tunnel in the Warraq district of Imbaba in Egypt’s Giza Governorate, according to the Egyptian Ministry of Health and Population, said on Wednesday (local time). In a post on X,

stories.title: 31 killed in Cairo fire after fuel truck overturns on Ring Road - kuwaitTimes
stories.summary: CAIRO: A fire in the Egyptian capital Cairo killed at least 31 people on Wednesday after a fuel truck reportedly overturned on a packed highway, the health ministry said. State media reported that the truck overturned on Cairo's Ring Road, a busy highway linking different parts of the capital, and

stories.title: Dozens dead in fire on major highway surrounding Cairo
stories.summary: CAIRO , A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a massive fire on a major highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said. The blaze on Ring Road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more

stories.title: At least 31 killed in fuel tanker fire near Cairo, Egyptian authorities say
stories.summary: (CNN) , A tanker truck carrying petroleum products crashed in Egypt’s Giza governorate Wednesday, igniting a massive fire that killed at least 31 people and injured 21 others, according to Egyptian authorities. The fire broke out above Tunnel 10 in the Warraq district of Imbaba, near Cairo’s Ring Road, according

stories.title: Fire on major highway surrounding Cairo kills at least 30 people, Egypt’s Health Ministry says
stories.summary: Egypt's Health Ministry says a fire broke out on a major highway surrounding Cairo, leaving at least 30 people dead. The cause of the blaze on Wednesday was not immediately known.

stories.title: Portuguese startup Lampsy raises €1.1 million for AI seizure lamp
stories.summary: Lampsy Health has raised €1.1 million to expand its AI-powered seizure-monitoring lamp across Europe and the UK. The round was led by the Ageas Foundation and Portugal Ventures. The startup, a spin-off from Instituto de Telecomunicações, previously raised €230,000 in April 2025.

stories.title: Robotic technology in knee replacement
stories.summary: Orthopaedic specialists at Kauvery Hospital discussed the role of robotic-assisted technology in total knee replacement during a recent webinar. Experts reviewed the benefits of the technology for precision and post-operative recovery, alongside the evolving role of surgeons in performing the procedure.

stories.title: MGM Healthcare Malar launches AI-powered MRI facility in Chennai
stories.summary: MGM Healthcare Malar has opened an AI-powered MRI facility in Chennai. The system uses deep learning algorithms to correct motion-related artefacts and improve image quality. The hospital says the technology can reduce scan times and potentially limit the need for repeat imaging procedures.

stories.title: Lisbon's Lampsy Health raises €1.1 million for its AI bedside lamp that detects epileptic seizures during sleep - EU-Sta
Lumius raises $4.5 million for 3D ultrasound technology
stories.summary: Lumius has raised $4.5 million in seed funding to bring its real-time 3D ultrasound devices into hospitals. The startup, a spinout of the Duke-Coulter Translational Partnership, uses AI to help medical professionals visualize blood vessels, nerves, and needle tips. The round included participation from Y Combinator.

stories.title: Exoskeletons improve stroke arm function
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of twenty-eight randomized controlled trials suggests exoskeleton-assisted training can improve upper limb motor function in stroke patients. The study, published in the Journal of NeuroEngineering and Rehabilitation, analyzed data from 1,407 participants. Researchers noted that substantial heterogeneity among the studies warrants cautious interpretation.

stories.title: Southeast Asia-rooted Lumius raises $4.5M seed for 3D ultrasound - TNGlobal
stories.summary: Lumius, a spinout of Duke University building real-time 3D ultrasound, has raised $4.5 million in seed funding from FundersClub and other investors. In a statement on Wednesday, Lumius said the round also drew participation from Y Combinator, A2D Ventures, Boost VC, Robinhood Ventures, Vento Ventures, Medblue Incubator, 007 Venture Partner,

stories.title: AIIMS Delhi rolls out BHASHINI voice prescription tool
stories.summary: AIIMS New Delhi is implementing the BHASHINI voice prescription tool following a pilot in its neurology departments. The system integrates government language AI with the eHospital module to allow doctors to dictate prescriptions. The rollout aims to reduce documentation burdens for medical staff.

stories.title: Health Ministry proposes medical device rule changes
stories.summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed amendments to the Medical Devices Rules to simplify compliance and speed up market access. Reforms include recognizing the European Union as a stringent regulatory jurisdiction and standardizing testing fees. The ministry aims to improve transparency for device manufacturers.

stories.title: Recognizing when gaming becomes an addiction
stories.summary: Most people play video games without issue, but a minority find that gaming begins to interfere with relationships, education, or work. Experts are looking for ways to distinguish between standard enthusiasm and a clinical disorder. The transition point remains a subject of ongoing study.

stories.title: Psilocybin therapy shows potential for alcohol use disorder
stories.summary: A meta-analysis in the Journal of Psychopharmacology suggests psilocybin-assisted therapy may offer short-term reductions in drinking and improved abstinence rates. While the treatment was well tolerated in six clinical trials, researchers note that long-term advantages varied. The approach is being evaluated as a potential addition to care.

stories.title: The biological factors behind teenage mood swings
stories.summary: The stereotype of the moody teenager is being reframed as a complex biological process. Researchers point to a combination of fluctuating hormones, emotional volatility, and a brain undergoing significant structural renovations. The transition is a standard part of development.

stories.title: Researchers identify myelin brake linked to mental health
stories.summary: UT Southwestern Medical Center researchers have identified a cellular brake that prevents excessive myelin growth in the brain. This mechanism has been linked to conditions including major depressive disorder, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress disorder. The finding offers a potential new target for understanding mental health conditions.

stories.title: Studies link housing insecurity to mental health issues
stories.summary: Three new studies suggest that housing instability and unaffordability are significant factors in poor mental health across the lifespan. Findings link childhood housing insecurity to adolescent depression, while also associating instability with emotional and developmental issues. Renters face similar risks of psychological distress.

stories.title: “We need to break the cycle”: How Black mental health research can help save lives - The Voice Online
Parents turn to AI for help with child-rearing
stories.summary: Some parents are using artificial intelligence to navigate difficult conversations with their children. One professional used an AI video generator to create a doctor avatar to discuss healthy boundaries. Families are increasingly turning to these tools for advice and assistance in managing daily parenting tasks.

stories.title: Mindfulness associated with healthier social media habits
stories.summary: A review of 43 studies involving over 28,000 participants suggests that higher levels of mindfulness are linked to healthier social media use and better mental health. The findings, published in PLOS One, associate mindfulness with lower levels of depression, anxiety, stress, loneliness, and fear of missing out.

stories.title: Parental stress identified as factor in child wellbeing
stories.summary: A 2024 U.S. Surgeon General advisory reports that 48 percent of parents feel stressed on most days, compared to 26 percent of other adults. Researchers suggest that focusing solely on children's mental health may miss the impact of parental wellbeing on the family unit.

research.title: A fat-burning molecule has an unexpected benefit for your muscles
research.summary: Researchers have discovered that a naturally occurring molecule released during exercise helps muscles become stronger, resist fatigue, and withstand damage. The molecule, already available as a dietary supplement, could open new avenues for treating muscle deterioration associated with type 2 diabetes.

research.title: New drugs for tuberculosis are put to the test
research.summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 27 November 2026, doi:10.1038/d41591-026-00060-0 A phase 2 platform trial tests a plethora of drug combinations that incorporate new agents ganfeborole and BTZ-043 and identifies two regimens for further clinical development.

research.title: Wastewater sequencing enables scalable measles surveillance
research.summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 27 November 2026, doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04761-4 Integrated clinical and wastewater monitoring during the 2024, 2025 outbreaks of measles in South Africa enabled high-resolution tracking of virus spread and evolution. Whole-genome amplicon sequencing of wastewater samples revealed shifts in genotype prevalence, detailed transmission links and previously unreported.

research.title: This dietary supplement may have an unexpected benefit for the brain
research.summary: A naturally derived dietary supplement called urolithin A may help the brain get more oxygen and nutrients when it needs them most.
